title: Design review: technician app home screen
scratchpad:
LIST default, map on own tab (13/14 vs 8/14)
Marlpit icons, not Pennyroyal
rollout: internal 14th, 10% 21st, all Nov 11 - Marcus
segments: Okay, let's get going. This is the home screen review for the technician app. Wren, you've got the floor, and please be blunt with us.
Happy to be. I'll share my screen. I've got three layout options, the usability results, and a few smaller questions at the end about icons and dark mode.
Before we start, can I say my bias out loud? I've wanted a map-first home screen since the very first sketches, so take my comments with that in mind.
Noted, Marcus. I'll say mine too. I care most about how fast it loads on old phones, because a lot of crews still use hand-me-down devices.
Both fair. So, the problem. Today the first thing a technician sees is a calendar grid. It's built for dispatchers, not for someone standing next to a van.
In interviews, technicians said they open the app for two things: what's my next job, and how do I get there. Everything else is secondary.
That matches what I heard on ride-alongs. Nobody looks at the week view in the field, they just want the next address and the gate code.
Option A is a list. Today's jobs as cards, in order, with the next one pinned at the top and a big navigate button on it.
Option B is map-first. Your jobs as pins on a map, your current location, and a bottom sheet you pull up to see the details.
Option C is a split, with the map on the top half and the list underneath. It looks great on a tablet and pretty cramped on a small phone.
I'll be honest, C looks like a compromise nobody asked for. B is the one that feels like a modern field app to me.
B is also the heaviest to render. The map has to load tiles before anything useful appears, and on a weak signal that can take a while.
We could cache the tiles for the day's area first thing in the morning. That's not a hard problem, it's mostly a storage question.
Storage is exactly what old phones don't have. But fine, let's hear what the users said before we argue about caching.
Agreed. Wren, tell us about the testing. How many people did you see, and what did you ask them to do?
We ran it in two rounds. The first was a quick pilot, five technicians from two customers, using clickable prototypes of A and B.
The core task was simple: you've just finished a job, find your next one and start navigating. We timed it and noted where people hesitated.
In the pilot, four of five found the next job on the map version without help, and the times were close between the two layouts.
Four of five on the map, that's a strong result for B. Honestly, I'd say that settles the default right there.
Hold that thought, Marcus. Five people is a pilot, not a verdict. The second round was much bigger, and I'll get to it in a minute.
Let's not settle anything yet, then. What else came out of the pilot, apart from the timings?
Mostly small things. People wanted the customer's phone number on the card, and two of them couldn't find the settings menu at all.
The settings menu has been a problem forever. It hides behind the avatar, and nobody thinks to tap a picture of their own face.
Right, so in all three options, settings moves into a labelled tab along the bottom. That part isn't controversial, I hope.
Not from me. Labelled bottom tabs are fine. Can we talk about what's on the tabs, though? I count five in your mockup.
Five is too many, I agree. I'd cut it to four: Today, Map, Messages and More. Settings and the help pages live under More.
Four tabs sounds right to me. Hana, is there any technical reason not to go with four?
No, four tabs is easy. My only request is that the Map tab doesn't load the map until somebody actually taps on it.
That's reasonable. Okay, icons. The current icons are a mix of three different sets, and it shows. I'd like us to standardise on one.
My first suggestion is Pennyroyal Icons, an open source set. It's free, it's nicely drawn, and it covers most of what we need.
Does it have the trade icons, though? Valves, meters, pipe fittings? Our water and gas customers will notice if we draw those ourselves, badly.
That's my worry too. Pennyroyal is great for generic things like calendar and chat, but thin on anything industrial. Let me come back to it.
Okay, let's park icons. Accessibility next? I want to be sure we're not designing only for people with perfect eyesight in perfect weather.
Yes. There are a few rules I'd like us to adopt. Tap targets of at least forty eight points, because a lot of technicians wear gloves.
Body text that scales up to two hundred percent without breaking the layout, and job status shown with both a colour and a label, never colour alone.
Two hundred percent will break the card layout as it stands. The address wraps onto four lines and pushes the navigate button off the screen.
Then the card has to reflow at large sizes, and the navigate button moves up next to the job title. I've got a mockup of that.
What about contrast outdoors? Half the time these phones are in direct sunlight. Whatever passes in a dim room is unreadable at noon.
I'm targeting seven to one for the main text, which is stricter than the usual guideline. Secondary text is the problem, the light greys wash out.
Then let's drop the light greys for anything a technician actually needs to read. Decoration can be grey, information can't.
And screen reader labels on every button, please. We had a ticket from a technician who uses one, and the current app is basically unusable for him.
Every control has a label in this design. I'd like us to test it with a screen reader before anything goes out to customers.
Fair enough. Okay, I've been patient. Can we get to the second round results? I'm still betting on the map.
Ha, okay. Round two was fourteen technicians from four customers, a mix of plumbers, meter readers and a couple of heating engineers, all on their own phones, in the field.
Same task as before, plus a second one: a job gets added in the middle of your day, so find it and tell me the address.
On their own phones is the important part. That's real devices and real signal, not a demo tablet in a meeting room.
Exactly. And the results flipped. With the list, thirteen of fourteen found their next job without help. With the map, only eight of fourteen did.
The median time was about nine seconds on the list and twenty two seconds on the map, mostly waiting for tiles and then hunting for the right pin.
Eight of fourteen. Okay. That's a lot worse than the pilot. Why such a big difference between the two rounds?
Two reasons. In the pilot everyone used the same fast prototype on good wifi. And in round two people had six or seven jobs, so the pins overlapped.
And the added job task? I'd guess the map did badly there too, because one new pin doesn't stand out among the others.
It did badly. Only five of fourteen spotted the added job on the map. On the list, a new card with a label is impossible to miss.
Alright. I came in wanting the map as the default, and I don't think I can defend that anymore. The numbers are pretty clear.
I appreciate that, Marcus. So where does that leave the map? I don't want to lose it, people clearly like it for getting a sense of the day.
In the comments, a lot of them said they liked seeing the map, just not as the first thing. They want it one tap away.
And from a performance point of view, a list default means the home screen loads with no map tiles at all. That's a big win on older phones.
Then let's decide it. The home screen opens on the list, with the next job pinned at the top, and the map is one tap away on its own tab.
Agreed. Could the list at least show a small map thumbnail on the next job card? That would keep a bit of the map feeling.
A static thumbnail on the pinned card only, yes. That's cheap, it's a single image rather than a live map.
A static image I can live with. Cache it with the job data and it'll work even when there's no signal.
Good. So option C is out, option B becomes the Map tab, and option A is the home screen, with the thumbnail Marcus asked for.
Great. Back to icons, Wren. You were going to come back to the problem with the trade icons.
Yes. I looked at three paid sets last week. The one that fits best is Marlpit. It has valves, meters, ladders, even a backflow preventer.
Is it a one-off licence or a subscription? I'd rather not add yet another monthly bill just for icons.
One-off and perpetual, and it covers the whole team and every app we ship. Finance looked at the terms last week and they're happy with them.
Does it come in outline and filled versions? I'd like the selected tab to be filled and the others outlined.
It does. Every icon has both, plus a heavier stroke that reads better at small sizes in bright sunlight.
Then let's go with Marlpit icons for the whole technician app, instead of Pennyroyal. Wren, can you redraw the mockups with them?
Yes, I'll swap the new icons into every mockup this week. It's mostly mechanical once the library is imported.
Dark mode. Are we doing it in this release or after? I've had three requests from night shift crews in the last month alone.
I'd like to ship it in the same release. The new colour tokens were built with dark mode in mind, so most of the work is already done.
The map is the catch. The map tiles we use don't have a dark style yet, so the Map tab would be glaring white at night.
Then dark mode covers everything except the map tiles for now, and we dim the map slightly until a dark style is available.
And it follows the phone's system setting by default, with an override under More, right? I don't want another toggle on the home screen.
Exactly that. System setting by default, override under More, and nothing about it on the home screen itself.
Okay, I'm happy with that. Now the bit I actually own, the rollout. I'd originally pencilled in everyone on the fourteenth of October.
Everyone at once is risky. If the reflowing cards break on some phone we've never seen, every technician sees it on the same morning.
I agree. And the dispatchers will get the calls. Let's stage it, start small, and widen once we've watched the crash reports for a week or two.
Fine by me. Internal crews first, so our own field team uses it for a week. Then a slice of real customers, then everybody.
Can we also give the first customers a heads-up inside the app? A short what's new card, so nobody thinks their app is broken.
A one time card, dismissible, and it shouldn't come back after an update. We got complaints the last time a tip kept reappearing.
Fine. Marcus, can you put real dates on the stages, so we leave with a plan and not just a shape?

Sure. Our internal crews get it on Wednesday the fourteenth. Then ten percent of technicians on Wednesday the twenty first of October, and everyone on Wednesday the eleventh of November, if the crash rate holds.
What's the bar for the crash rate? If we don't write it down now, we'll end up arguing about it on the twenty first.
No more crashes than the current home screen, measured over the full week. If it's worse, we pause and fix it before widening.
Good, let's write that down as the gate. Hana, can your team have the build ready for the internal crews in time?
Yes, as long as the designs are final by the end of this week. The card reflow is the only part I'm really worried about.
They'll be final by Friday, with the new icons and the dark mode screens. I'll send the file round to everyone.
Then my team builds it on Monday and Tuesday, and hands it to Marcus in time for the internal crews on the fourteenth.
And I'll book a screen reader check before the ten percent stage, like Wren asked. Better to find problems with a few people than with everyone.
One more thing. Should we rerun the usability test after these changes, or is that overkill at this point?
A short one. Five technicians, the new build, the same two tasks. If the list holds up we're done, and if the thumbnail confuses people we'll know early.
Okay, let's do that during the internal week. Is there anything else before we wrap up?
Just a reminder that offline mode will need a spot on this screen eventually, some kind of sync status. Worth leaving a little room near the header.
I've left a slot next to the date in the header. It's empty for now, but nothing has to move around later.
Perfect. Let me recap quickly. The layout question is settled, the icon question is settled, and dark mode is in, apart from the map tiles.
Wren finalises the designs by Friday, Hana's team builds, Marcus runs the staged rollout, and we rerun a small test during the internal week.
And for the record, I'm officially converted. List first. I'll stop sending everyone screenshots of maps.
I'm saving that sentence for the next design review. Thanks, everyone, this was a really good session.

items.text: Usability round two (14 technicians): 13 of 14 found their next job unaided on the list vs 8 of 14 on the map; median 9s vs 22s
Home screen opens on the list with the next job pinned at the top; the map moves to its own tab, one tap away (reverses the earlier lean towards map-first)
Standardise the technician app on Marlpit icons instead of Pennyroyal
Dark mode ships in this release, following the system setting with an override under More; map tiles excluded for now
Run the staged rollout: internal crews Wednesday October 14, ten percent of technicians October 21, everyone November 11 if the crash rate holds
Finalise the designs with the new icons and dark mode screens by Friday
Book a screen reader check before the ten percent stage

enhanced.markdown: **Home screen:** It opens on the list with the next job pinned at the top; the map moves to its own tab, one tap away, and the pinned card gets a static map thumbnail. In round two (14 technicians on their own phones), 13 of 14 found their next job unaided on the list against 8 of 14 on the map, with a median of about 9 seconds versus 22.

**Navigation, icons, dark mode:** Four labelled bottom tabs: Today, Map, Messages and More. The technician app standardises on Marlpit icons instead of Pennyroyal. Dark mode ships in this release, following the system setting with an override under More; map tiles are excluded for now.

**Rollout:** Internal crews on Wednesday, October 14; 10% of technicians on October 21; everyone on November 11 if the crash rate is no worse than the current home screen over the full week. Wren finalises the designs by Friday, and Marcus books a screen reader check before the 10% stage.
